newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends at 35.83/84 on late RBI dlr bids.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends at 35.83/84 on late RBI dlr bids.

text.p: Dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday evening helped the rupee close unchanged at 35.83/84 against the dollar, dealers said.
The rupee saw two-way movement on Friday, swinging from a high of 35.81 to a low of 35.84, dealers said.
The day opened in the aftermath of the rupee's sharp movement on Thursday triggered by Bank of Baroda 's dollar purchase which pushed the rupee to 35.86/87 level.
The market was short on dollars but dealers did not expect large dollar demand on Friday except for some left-over demand from Bank of Baroda which stole the thunder on Thursday.
The rupee edged up gradually to 35.81 level but rallied in afternoon trade to 35.835 level before softening again.
The RBI entered the market towards the close, checking prices and buying small amounts from a handful of banks.

"The market was not long or comfortable," said the chief dealer at a leading bank in Bombay. "The banks which were hit by RBI, hit SBI (State Bank of India) which in turn hit others, leading to a chain reaction," he said.
This helped the dollar close the day at 35.83/84 rupees.

Forward dollar premiums drifted down on continued exporter sales to take advantage of a mild rally in spot dollar, dealers said. The six month annualised forward premium closed the day at 4.21 percent compared with the previous close of 4.30 percent.
